text: As they ran, they heard shots behind them, and when they reached the hut, there was a brief struggle with its owner before Arsat could push the canoe into the water. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking back once, Arsat saw his brother running toward them across the open ground with many men close behind him, and he heard him shout, I am coming. <break time="0.8s" /> Then I looked at her, Tuan, and I pushed the canoe into deep water, said Arsat, and though my brother called my name three times, I never turned my head. <break time="0.8s" /> She was there with me, and for her I would have faced all men, Arsat went on, and the white man, after a silence, said quietly, We all love our brothers. <break time="0.8s" /> Arsat cried out that he had only wanted peace in his own heart, and then he fell silent, while the darkness slowly faded and a white mist covered the lagoon. <break time="0.8s" /> When the sun rose above the trees, the mist broke apart, and a white eagle rose over the lagoon and soared upward until it vanished into the bright sky. <break time="0.8s" /> At that moment Arsat stumbled out of the house and stood by the white man, and in a dull voice he said only, She burns no more. <break time="0.8s" /> He said that he would neither eat nor sleep in this house again, for he was going back now to where his brother had fallen, though he could see nothing ahead. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking back from his departing boat, the white man saw Arsat standing alone in the sunshine, staring through the light of a cloudless day into the hopeless darkness of the world.
